tip: 'Masuk akal' = to make sense, literally 'enters reason': 'tidak masuk akal' = unreasonable.
'Kelihatannya' = it looks like, built from 'lihat' (see): 'kelihatannya kamu lelah'.
'Sepertinya' = it seems, from 'seperti' (like): 'sepertinya dia sibuk' = it seems he's busy.
'Sepertinya' = it seems. In Jakarta speech you'll hear 'kayaknya' for this everywhere – recognize it, model 'sepertinya'.
'Sepertinya enak' = 'that sounds nice' – a common way to float a food idea.
'Saling' makes almost any verb mutual: 'saling membantu' = help each other, 'saling kenal' = know each other, 'saling percaya' = trust each other.
'Ikut' + feeling = to share it: 'saya ikut sedih' = I'm sad for you too.
'Se-' + quality = as ... as: 'seindah foto' = as beautiful as the photo.
'Bangga pada' + person = proud of: 'bangga pada tim ini' = proud of this team.
'Padahal' = even though / when in fact: 'belum pulang, padahal sudah malam'.
'Berharap' needs a subject ('saya berharap...'); 'semoga' opens a wish on its own: 'Semoga lancar!'
'Rezeki' = livelihood, blessings – a warm everyday wish word: 'diberi rezeki'.
'Sampai dengan selamat' = arrive safely – a standard send-off for travelers.
'Lebih suka' X 'daripada' Y = to prefer X to Y: 'lebih suka kereta daripada pesawat'.
'Katanya' = he/she says, they say: 'katanya lebih nikmat' = he says it tastes better.
'Yang penting' = the main thing is: 'yang penting kamu selamat' = what matters is you're safe.
'Bagaimana menurut kamu?' = What do you think? Literally 'how according to you?'.
In formal settings (meetings, clients) use 'Anda' instead of 'kamu': 'Bagaimana menurut Anda?'
'Kurang setuju' softens disagreement – politer than a flat 'tidak setuju'.
'Sebagian ... sebagian lagi' = some ... others: 'sebagian setuju, sebagian lagi menolak'.
'Menyampaikan' is from 'sampai' (arrive, reach; the 's' becomes 'ny' after 'me-'): to voice an opinion is to make it reach people.
'Suasana hati' = mood – literally 'atmosphere of the heart'.
'Lipat' means fold, so 'dua kali lipat' = 'two times folded', like English twofold. It scales: 'tiga kali lipat' = tripled. 'Naik dua kali lipat' = doubled.
Doubling an adjective can soften it into a gradual manner: 'pelan' = slow, 'pelan-pelan' = little by little. 'Pelan-pelan rasa takutnya hilang' = the fear slowly faded.
'Apa pun' = whatever / no matter what: 'apa pun pendapat orang' = whatever people think.
'Semakin ... semakin' = the more ... the more: 'semakin lama, semakin suka' = the longer, the more (I) like it.
'Semakin' + adjective alone = getting more and more X: 'semakin tinggi' = higher and higher.
'Ke-...-an' here turns a verb into a noun: 'berangkat' = to depart, 'keberangkatan' = departure.
'Makin' is the everyday spoken short form of 'semakin': 'makin siang' = the later in the day.
'Sama' + adjective + '-nya' + 'dengan' = as ... as: 'sama mahalnya dengan' = as expensive as.
